Destroyed-workspace backup retention: workspace records gain a server-stamped `destroyed_at` (set on the destroyed transition, kept across updates, cleared on resurrection; existing destroyed rows stamped at migration time so pre-feature tombstones get the full 30-day rollout grace), served as a response-only field on the `/sync/records` wire so clients age their local reap countdowns against the server's clock, and an hourly `backup_retention_reap` cron deletes destroyed records' backup buckets (bounded, resumable emptying via new R2 object list/delete ops) and then the rows themselves once they age past the 30-day window.

Workspace-backup buckets are protected structurally: `POST /buckets` reserves the `host-` short-name shape (refused without a matching workspace record), and `DELETE /buckets/{name}` refuses a workspace-backup bucket whose record is still ACTIVE. Orphan buckets (no record at all) age from a first-seen stamp in the new `orphan_backup_buckets` table.

New public `GET /policies/destroyed-workspace-backups` endpoint serves the retention window; new `POST /admin/sweep/backup-retention` admin trigger runs a reap pass on demand with `?dry_run=1` (candidate list, no deletion) and an admin-only `?window_seconds=` override.
